definitions.explanation: A house or building constructed with only one floor, no upper stories. Often used in real estate listings and discussions of housing preference.

examples.english: I live in a single-story house.
My grandfather built a single-story house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}ったら→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦{階段|かいだん}→階段：00782_kaidan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧{平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}て⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}みたい→住む：00673_sumu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}っている→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: When I get older, I'd like to live in a single-story house with no stairs.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{平屋|ひらや}→平屋：15682_hiraya⟧ (single-story building) + {建|だ}て (constructed as). Often shortened to just ⟦{平屋|ひらや}→平屋：15682_hiraya⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧: single-story house
- {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}て⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{建|た}てる→建てる：01189_tateru⟧: to build a single-story house
- {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}て⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}む→住む：00673_sumu⟧: to live in a single-story house

CULTURAL NOTE:
Single-story homes are increasingly popular among older Japanese couples and retirees because they avoid stairs and are easier to maintain. They are also associated with rural and traditional housing.

RELATED WORDS:
- 〜⟦{階|かい}{建|だ}て→階建て：29226_kaidate⟧: ~storied (general counter pattern for number of floors)
- ⟦{二|に}{階|かい}{建|だ}て→二階建て：03001_nikaidate⟧: two-story (the most common urban housing form)
